title: Digital access with patron agency
idea: Help adults at a public library decide how to approach an unfamiliar online service without surrendering control or disclosing sensitive information. First investigate access, staffing and service design barriers, then develop a small fictional task-planning workbench. Use an invented community event registration task requiring no real accounts or personal information. Let a patron choose online, staffed or paper assistance, explain an next action, respond to an interruption or confusing requirement, and revise a plan. The goal is supported choice and help-seeking, not making everyone independently complete an online task.
domain: Public library digital participation and community service access
people: Adult patrons with varied literacy, languages and digital access; librarians, volunteers and service owners; none are participants in this demonstration.
constraints: Never request real passwords, identifiers, contact details, account information or actual service records. No eligibility advice, banking, legal or medical guidance. No patron skill score or deficit label. Shared computers and limited staff time are constraints to examine, not assumed resources. Include a paper or staffed alternative, a visible way to clear or conceal fictional notes, and descriptive feedback whose limits are clear. Patron and librarian review and any actual pilot remain pending. Require a complete small interactive HTML candidate and a meaningful revision after a challenge.
